concepts.title: Two-Component Cloning System and Vector Features
concepts.definition: Gene cloning pairs a carrier with a workhorse: the insert is spliced into a vector, the recombinant DNA enters a host, and the host's enzymes multiply the construct; E. coli K12, doubling about every twenty minutes, leads the prokaryotic hosts with Bacillus subtilis for secreted proteins and yeast for eukaryotes, while a usable vector must stay small, carry an origin of replication, offer unique restriction sites and bear at least one selectable marker such as tetracycline or ampicillin resistance.
concepts.key_idea: Host supplies the replication machinery, vector supplies the control sequences - and four features make a vector worth using.
question_patterns: describe the two key components of recombinant DNA technology with a schematic of gene cloning
list the four features every cloning vector must possess

solution_steps.explain: Isolate the insert, ligate it into the cut vector, and transform the host.
Small size, an ori for autonomous replication, unique cloning sites and a selectable marker are non-negotiable.
Match host to purpose - fast propagation in E. coli, secretion in Bacillus, eukaryotic folding in yeast.

concepts.title: Plasmid Copy Number and Vector Engineering
concepts.definition: Plasmids are circular extrachromosomal DNAs from a few kilobases to over a hundred: relaxed high-copy plasmids escape chromosome control to reach ten to thirty copies per cell and stronger screening signals, whereas stringent low-copy plasmids hold one or a few; engineers then trim and recombine natural plasmids - nine-kilobase pBR313 with tetR and ampR lost its non-essential bulk to become the 4,361 bp pBR322, and later pUC19 at 2.686 kb added a synthetic polylinker and blue-white selection through lacZ.
concepts.key_idea: Subtract the engineered size from the natural one to price the deleted non-essential DNA.
question_patterns: pBR313 measured about 9 kb and pBR322 was trimmed to 4361 bp - how many base pairs were deleted
what percent of the pBR313 DNA was removed during construction of pBR322
differentiate relaxed replication of high copy plasmids from stringent replication of low copy plasmids

solution_steps.explain: Deletion equals the natural size minus the engineered size.
Deleted bases over the original size times one hundred.

concepts.title: Lambda Phage Genome and Its Vectors
concepts.definition: Lambda's linear 48,490 bp genome carries twelve-base cohesive ends that anneal inside E. coli to close a 48,502 bp circle at the cos site; about one-third of the middle region, the lysogeny genes, is dispensable for lytic growth, so vectors replace that stretch with inserts sized 38-52 kbp for packaging - insertion vectors such as lambda gt10 and gt11 taking up to about 7 kbp, and replacement vectors like EMBL3 trading their stuffer for 20 kbp inserts.
concepts.key_idea: Add the paired cohesive bases to the linear length for the circular genome, and divide by three to find the replaceable middle.
question_patterns: a lambda genome of 48490 bp linear DNA closes through 12-base cohesive ends - compute the circular length

solution_steps.explain: The two complementary cohesive ends pair, adding their overlap to the length.
One-third of the genome, the lysogeny region, can be swapped for inserts.

concepts.title: M13 Filamentous Phage Vectors
concepts.definition: M13 threads a 6.4 kb single-stranded circular genome through a tube-shaped capsid, infecting only F-pilus-bearing E. coli without lysing them; inside, the strand becomes a double-stranded replicative form exploited for cloning inserts into the non-essential intergenic region, and vectors like M13mp18 add blue-white screening while yielding abundant single-stranded template.
concepts.key_idea: Clone into the intergenic region of the replicative form and harvest single-stranded DNA from the medium without killing the host.
question_patterns: why does bacteriophage M13 infect only E. coli cells carrying the F plasmid

solution_steps.explain: M13 attaches only to F-pilus-bearing cells and injects its single-stranded circle.
Host enzymes build the replicative form, which serves as the cloning substrate.
Packaged single-stranded genomes leave through the membrane without lysis.

worked_examples.q: M13 infects only E. coli bearing which structure: the F-pilus or a flagellum?

concepts.title: Cosmids and Phasmids as Hybrid Vectors
concepts.definition: Two hybrids stretch cloning capacity: a cosmid grafts as little as 250 bp of lambda DNA carrying the cos junction onto plasmid functions, letting recombinants of up to about 45 kbp be packaged in vitro into phage heads yet propagate as plasmids; a phasmid keeps whole lambda lytic genes at its ends around a central plasmid, replicating as a phage unless a lambda repressor gene flips it to plasmid mode.
concepts.key_idea: Cos sites win phage packaging, plasmid ori wins propagation - combine both and large inserts travel either way.
question_patterns: how many base pairs of lambda DNA suffice to provide the cos junction of a cosmid
differentiate a cosmid from a phasmid on the basis of the lambda DNA each carries

which selectable features does a typical cosmid borrow from its plasmid part

solution_steps.explain: Cosmids: plasmid ori, markers, polylinker plus a cos segment; phasmids: full lambda lytic arms around a plasmid middle.
Cosmids always propagate as plasmids; phasmids choose phage or plasmid mode by the repressor gene.
Cosmid inserts reach about 45 kbp thanks to in vitro packaging.

worked_examples.q: A cosmid grafts lambda's what onto plasmid functions: the cos junction or its tail?

concepts.title: Artificial Chromosomes YAC BAC and PAC
concepts.definition: Eukaryotic introns force cloning of huge fragments, so artificial chromosomes were built: yeast artificial chromosomes string two telomeres, a centromere, an ARS origin and markers into a linear yeast chromosome carrying 200-500 kb inserts while keeping a circular bacterial form; bacterial and phage artificial chromosomes extend the same idea from plasmid and phage parts, with capacities stepping from plasmid's ten kilobases up to about half a megabase.
concepts.key_idea: Subtract the capacity floor from the ceiling to size each vector class, and average the two for a typical insert.

solution_steps.explain: The range width shows how flexible the vector is.
The midpoint estimates a typical clonable insert.

concepts.title: Expression Vectors and Heterologous Expression
concepts.definition: Expression vectors do more than carry DNA - an inducible promoter upstream, a ribosome binding site, unique insertion sites and a downstream terminator wrap the cloned gene into an expression cassette that the host transcribes and translates on command; eukaryotic genes expressed in prokaryotes must arrive intron-free and need no post-translational dressing such as glycosylation to work.
concepts.key_idea: Promoter before, terminator after, inducible control throughout - and intron-free inserts when the host cannot splice.
question_patterns: label the components of an expression cassette in an expression vector

why is an expression vector sometimes called a sandwich expression vector

solution_steps.explain: Promoter-operator, ribosome binding site, polylinker and terminator bracket the insert.
Splicing is absent in prokaryotes, so the insert must be intron-free.
Proteins needing glycosylation or other modifications fail without a suitable host.

worked_examples.q: Eukaryotic genes expressed in prokaryotes must arrive without what: introns or exons?

concepts.title: Shuttle Vectors between Two Hosts
concepts.definition: Shuttle vectors pack two origins of replication and dual selection systems so one construct lives in E. coli for engineering and in yeast, plant or animal cells for expression, with only one origin active in any given host; most eukaryotic vectors are in fact such shuttles built by recombinant DNA methods.
concepts.key_idea: Two origins, two markers, one plasmid - build in bacteria, express in the eukaryote.
question_patterns: why does a shuttle vector carry two origins of replication and how are they used

solution_steps.explain: One bacterial ori and one eukaryotic origin, only one active per host.
Antibiotic resistance for bacteria and a eukaryotic selectable gene with promoter and poly-A signal.
Manipulate in E. coli, then transfer to the eukaryotic host where the second origin takes over.

worked_examples.q: How many origins of replication does a shuttle vector pack: two or none?
